chase_cards.name: Victory Ring
chase_cards.why: This is a chase because Battle Road memory changes shape here. Instead of a personalized No.1/No.2/No.3 Trainer portrait object, Victory Ring is a reusable winner-only tool: a card whose text says only official tournament winners may use it, and whose distribution still encodes region, age division, and podium finish.

key_artists.name: Takumi Akabane
key_artists.why: Akabane is not just a name on an illustration line; he sits inside the assembly of the TCG itself. Bulbapedia identifies him as a former Creatures R&D director, a co-creator of the Pokémon TCG with Tsunekazu Ishihara and Kouichi Ooyama, and the TCG creative director from 2001 to 2008. Victory Ring therefore carries both an artist credit and an apparatus credit.

claims.text: The local catalog models Battle Road Spring 2003 winner prize as one unnumbered promotional source row containing Victory Ring at source index 257.
Bulbapedia says Victory Ring was awarded to the top three competitors from each age division in each regional Japanese Battle Road Spring 2003 tournament held between March and April 2003.
Bulbapedia lists Battle Road Spring 2003 conferences at Hokkaido, Kanto A, Kansai, Tohoku, Chubu, Kyushu, Kanto B, and Chugoku/Shikoku between March 23 and April 6, 2003.

Bulbapedia gives Victory Ring's rule text as usable only by official tournament winners, then lets the player reveal Prize cards, exchange any number into the deck, shuffle, and set replacement Prize cards from the top of the deck.

Bulbapedia says the same 2003-2004 Victory Ring print was awarded again at Battle Road Autumn 2003, Battle Road Spring 2004, and Battle Road Autumn 2004, while 2005-2006 used a holographic Pikachu version with different artwork by the same illustrator.
Bulbapedia identifies Victory Ring as illustrated by Takumi Akabane and places Victory Ring among Akabane's miscellaneous promotional card illustrations.

Bulbapedia says Takumi Akabane was a former Creatures research and development director, was credited with creating the Pokémon TCG alongside Tsunekazu Ishihara and Kouichi Ooyama, and acted as TCG creative director from 2001 to 2008.
Bulbapedia says Victory Ring cards awarded between 2003 and 2004 were presented in framed certificates that featured the event name, regional tournament, age division, and winner name.
Bulbapedia estimates 189 copies of the 2003-2004 print based on regional tournament distribution; this is a broad print estimate, not an official Spring 2003 copy count for this row.

As judged collector texture, Victory Ring matters because it turns winner status into a playable, winner-only mechanism: the trophy is no longer only a named portrait or certificate but a card that acts on Prize cards while declaring who is allowed to use it.

Agents should preserve Victory Ring / 勝利のリング identity, source index 257, Battle Road Spring 2003 winner-prize route, top-three-per-age-division distribution, Takumi Akabane credit, framed-certificate context, and non-equivalence with Victory Orb, Victory Medal, 2005-2006 Pikachu Victory Ring, Autumn 2003/2004 copies, or generic trophy listings before accepting a match.

narrative.human_title: Battle Road Spring 2003 Victory Ring: the trophy becomes a playable rule
narrative.why_it_matters: Victory Ring is a hinge. The 2002 trophies remembered people by name, photograph, and place; this card remembers winners by giving them a strange little permission in the game itself. It says: only official tournament winners may use this. That line is pure apparatus. Region, age division, framed certificate, winner name, and Takumi Akabane's TCG-building hand all gather around a card that turns victory into a playable object.

narrative.human_title: Victory Ring, Spring 2003: permission printed as a card
narrative.why_it_matters: The line that matters is almost ceremonial: only official tournament winners may use this card. Victory Ring is collectible because it is scarce, yes, but the deeper pull is stranger. It is a card about being allowed to play a card, a little loop where organized play recognizes itself. For the catalog, that means title, event route, certificate context, and non-Pikachu 2003-2004 artwork must stay attached.
